metadata.title: NEW PROXIMAL POINT ALGORITHMS FOR CONVEX MINIMIZATION*

items.name: Quadratic model sequence and $\beta_k$
items.statement: We define the quadratic functions $\varphi_{k}(x)$, $k \geq 0$, recursively, as follows: $$\varphi_ {0} (x) := f (x _ {0}) + \frac {A}{2} \left\| x - x _ {0} \right\| ^ {2},$$ $$\begin{aligned} \varphi_ {k + 1} (x) :&= (1 - \alpha_ {k}) \varphi_ {k} (x) \tag {2.7} \\ + \alpha_ {k} (f (J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) + \langle (y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) / \lambda_ {k}, x - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k} \rangle). \end{aligned}$$ Here $A$ and $\lambda_k$ are positive numbers and $\alpha_k$ is a number in the interval [0,1). The point $x_0$ is feasible, that is, $f(x_0) < \infty$. Here the point $y_k \in \mathbb{R}^n$ can be arbitrary. Defining $$\beta_ {k} = \prod_ {j = 0} ^ {k - 1} (1 - \alpha_ {j}), \tag {2.2}$$ we have $\varphi_ {k} (x) - f (x) \leq \beta_ {k} (\varphi_ {0} (x) - f (x)). \tag {2.3}$

items.name: Objective assumptions and feasibility
items.statement: The objective $f:H\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous and convex. A point $x$ is feasible when $f(x)<+\infty$. These are the standing assumptions of the minimization problem (1.1).

items.name: Proximal mapping $J_\lambda$
items.statement: The classical proximal point algorithm is based on the notion of proximal mapping $J_{\lambda}$, $$J _ {\lambda} x := \arg \min _ {z \in \mathbb {R} ^ {n}} \left\{f (z) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda} \left\| z - x \right\| ^ {2} \right\}, \tag {1.2}$$ introduced earlier by Moreau [12].

items.name: Convex subdifferential qualification
items.statement:
For a proper convex function $f$, the convex subdifferential at a feasible point $x$ is

$$
\partial f(x)=\{g:f(z)\geq f(x)+\langle g,z-x\rangle\text{ for every }z\}.
$$

items.name: THE SECOND PROXIMAL POINT ALGORITHM
items.statement: Initialization. Choose a point $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and a constant $\lambda>0$. Define $y_1:=x_0$, $\lambda_1:=\lambda$, and $\beta_1:=1$. Step $\mathbf k$, $k\geq1$. Choose $\lambda_k\geq\lambda_{k-1}$ and define $$\beta_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4\beta_k^2}}2, \tag{6.1}$$ $$x_k=J_{\lambda_k}y_k:=\arg\min_{x\in\mathbf R^n}\{f(x)+(1/(2\lambda_k))\|x-y_k\|^2\}, \tag{6.2}$$ $$y_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{\beta_k-1}{\beta_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1})+\frac{\beta_k}{\beta_{k+1}}(x_k-y_k). \tag{6.3}$$

items.name: Augmented function $\phi_k$
items.statement: The point $x_{k+1}$ is thus the exact minimum of the augmented function $$\phi_ {k} (z) := f (z) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda_ {k}} \left\| z - y _ {k} \right\| ^ {2}. \tag {3.2}$$

items.name: Proximal objective and proximal minimizers
items.statement:
For $\lambda>0$ and center $y$, the proximal objective is

$$
P_{\lambda,y}(z)=f(z)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|z-y\|^2.
$$

A proximal point is a point attaining $\min_z P_{\lambda,y}(z)$, equivalently an element of the proximal mapping $J_\lambda y$ in (1.2).

items.name: Subdifferential residual
items.statement:
For a point $x$ with nonempty subdifferential, the subdifferential residual is the distance from the origin to $\partial f(x)$:

$$
r_f(x)=\inf\{\|g\|:g\in\partial f(x)\}.
$$

items.name: Strong convexity in subgradient form
items.statement:
A convex function $g$ is strongly convex with modulus $m>0$ when every $s\in\partial g(x)$ satisfies

$$
g(y)\geq g(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+\frac m2\|y-x\|^2
$$

for all $x,y$.

items.name: Subdifferentiation formula for a proximal minimizer
items.statement: Referenced as: Since $J_{\lambda_k}y_k$ is the minimizer in (1.6), $0 \in \partial f(J_{\lambda_k}y_k) + (J_{\lambda_k}y_k-y_k)/\lambda_k$, that is, $$(y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) / \lambda_ {k} \in \partial f (J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}). \tag {2.8}$$
items.proof: Cited from: R. T. Rockafellar, Monotone operators and the proximal point algorithm, SIAM J. Control Optim., 14 (1976), pp. 877-898, p. 889.

items.name: DEFINITION 3.1
items.statement: We will say that $x_{k+1}$ is an approximation minimizer of $\phi_k$ if the following criterion $\mathbf{A}'$ in Rockafellar [18, pp. 880] is satisfied: $$\rho (0, \partial \phi_ {k} (x _ {k + 1})) \leqslant \frac {\varepsilon_ {k}}{\lambda_ {k}}. \tag {$A^{\prime$}}$$ Note that if $f$ is differentiable, condition $\mathbf{A}'$ means that $\|\phi_k'(x_{k+1})\|\leq\varepsilon_k/\lambda_k$.

items.name: Estimate-quadratic recurrences
items.statement:
The estimate functions used in Section 2 have the quadratic representation

$$
\phi_k(x)=\phi_k^*+\frac{A_k}{2}\|x-\nu_k\|^2,
$$

with the scalar and center recurrences obtained from (2.7), including $A_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)A_k$ and the corresponding update of $\nu_{k+1}$.

items.name: Strong-convexity inequality
items.statement: Referenced as: If $g$ is strongly convex with modulus $m$, $w\in\partial g(u)$, then $g(v)-g(u)\geq\langle w,v-u\rangle+(m/2)\|v-u\|^2$.
items.proof: Cited from: R. T. Rockafellar, Monotone operators and the proximal point algorithm, SIAM J. Control Optim., 14 (1976), pp. 877-898, Proposition 6(c).

items.name: LEMMA 2.1
items.statement: For all $k \geq 0$, the quadratic functions $\varphi_k(x)$ defined above satisfy inequality (2.1), that is, $$\varphi_ {k + 1} (x) - f (x) \leq (1 - \alpha_ {k}) (\varphi_ {k} (x) - f (x)).$$
items.proof: Proof. Since $J_{\lambda_k}y_k$ is the minimizer in (1.6), we have by the subdifferentiation formula (see Rockafellar [18, pp. 889]), $0 \in \partial f(J_{\lambda_k}y_k) + (J_{\lambda_k}y_k-y_k)/\lambda_k$, that is, (2.8). Since $f$ is convex, for any $x \in \mathbf{R}^n$, we have $$f (x) \geq f (J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) + \langle (y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) / \lambda_ {k}, x - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k} \rangle . \tag {2.9}$$ Thus $$\begin{aligned} \varphi_ {k + 1} (x) - f (x) &= (1 - \alpha_ {k}) (\varphi_ {k} (x) - f (x)) \\ &+ \alpha_ {k} (f (J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) + \langle (y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) / \lambda_ {k}, x - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k} \rangle - f (x)) \\ &\leq (1 - \alpha_ {k}) (\varphi_ {k} (x) - f (x)). \end{aligned}$$ □

items.name: THEOREM 6.1
items.statement: The proximal point algorithm stated above possesses the global convergence rate estimate $$f(x_k)-\min_{x\in\mathbf R^n}f(x)\leqslant\frac1{\lambda(k+1)^2}\rho(x_0,X^*)^2, \tag{6.4}$$ where $X^*$ is the set of minimizers of $f$.
items.proof: Proof. From (2.8) and (6.2), $(y_{i+1}-x_{i+1})/\lambda_{i+1}\in\partial f(x_{i+1})$. Convexity gives (6.5) and (6.6). Equation (6.1) implies $\beta_{i+1}(\beta_{i+1}-1)=\beta_i^2$ (6.7). Defining $W_i:=f(x_i)-f(x^*)$, multiplying (6.5) and (6.6) as in the paper and adding gives (6.10). The polarization identity gives (6.11). Define $\theta_i:=\beta_{i+1}(x_i-y_{i+1})+x^*-x_i$ (6.12); (6.3) gives (6.13). Thus summing (6.14) yields (6.15). Applying (6.6) for $i=0$ yields (6.16), hence $$\beta_k^2W_k\leqslant\frac1{4\lambda}\|x_0-x^*\|^2. \tag{6.17}$$ Since induction gives $\beta_k\cong(k+1)/2$, and $x^*\in X^*$ is arbitrary, the theorem follows. ☐

items.name: LEMMA 3.1
items.statement: Let $\phi_k^*=\min_{z\in\mathbf R^n}\phi_k(z)$. If $x_{k+1}$ satisfies condition $\mathbf A'$, then $$\frac1{2\lambda_k}\|x_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_k}y_k\|^2\leq\phi_k(x_{k+1})-\phi_k^*\leq\frac{\varepsilon_k^2}{2\lambda_k}. \tag{3.4}$$
items.proof: Proof. $J_{\lambda_k}y_k$ is the exact minimizer of $\phi_k$. Since $\phi_k$ is strongly convex with modulus $1/\lambda_k$ and $0\in\partial\phi_k(J_{\lambda_k}y_k)$, Proposition 6(c) gives the first inequality. Choose $w_k\in\partial\phi_k(x_{k+1})$ with $\|w_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k/\lambda_k$. The same proposition gives $$\phi_k(J_{\lambda_k}y_k)-\phi_k(x_{k+1})\geq-\frac{\varepsilon_k}{\lambda_k}\|J_{\lambda_k}y_k-x_{k+1}\|+\frac1{2\lambda_k}\|J_{\lambda_k}y_k-x_{k+1}\|^2\geq-\frac{\varepsilon_k^2}{2\lambda_k}.$$ This proves the lemma. $\square$

items.name: LEMMA 3.2
items.statement: If, for some $k\geq0$, $x_k$ satisfies $$f(x_k)\leq\varphi_k^*+\delta_k, \tag{3.6}$$ then for any $y_k\in\mathbf R^n$, $\lambda_k>0$, and $\alpha_k\in[0,1)$, $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{k+1}^*+(1-\alpha_k)\delta_k&\geq f(J_{\lambda_k}y_k)+\frac1{2\lambda_k}\left(2-\frac{\alpha_k^2}{A_{k+1}\lambda_k}\right)\|y_k-J_{\lambda_k}y_k\|^2\tag{3.7}\\&+\frac1{\lambda_k}\langle y_k-J_{\lambda_k}y_k,(1-\alpha_k)x_k+\alpha_k\nu_k-y_k\rangle.\end{aligned}$$
items.proof: Its proof is similar to that of the original Theorem 2.1.

items.name: THEOREM 2.1
items.statement: If, for some $k \geq 0$, $x_k$ satisfies the inequality (2.4), that is, $f(x_k) \leq \varphi_k^*$, then for any $y_k \in \mathbf{R}^n$, $\lambda_k > 0$, and $\alpha_k \in [0,1)$, the following inequality holds: $$Replace \cong with \geq or \ge$$ $$+ \frac {1}{\lambda_ {k}} \langle y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}, (1 - \alpha_ {k}) x _ {k} + \alpha_ {k} \nu_ {k} - y _ {k} \rangle .$$
items.proof: Proof. We obtain from (2.7), (2.10), and (2.11) the displayed calculation (2.14). Since by assumption $\varphi_k^* \geq f(x_k)$, we obtain from (2.9) the displayed inequality (2.15). The term $(1-\alpha_k)x_k+\alpha_k\nu_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_k}y_k$ is decomposed as stated in the paper; substitution of (2.12) gives (2.16), and substitution into the quadratic term gives (2.17). We obtain (2.13) by using lines (2.16) and (2.17) in (2.15). This proves the theorem. $\square$

items.name: COROLLARY 2.1
items.statement: If, in Theorem 2.1, we choose $$y _ {k} = (1 - \alpha_ {k}) x _ {k} + \alpha_ {k} \nu_ {k}, \tag {2.18}$$ then $$\varphi_ {k + 1} ^ {*} \geq f (J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k}) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda_ {k}} \left(2 - \frac {\alpha_ {k} ^ {2}}{A _ {k + 1} \lambda_ {k}}\right) \| y _ {k} - J _ {\lambda_ {k}} y _ {k} \| ^ {2}. \tag {2.19}$$

items.name: COROLLARY 3.1
items.statement: If $x_{k+1}$ is chosen according to criterion $\mathbf{A}'$, then $$\|x_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_k}y_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k. \tag{3.5}$$
items.proof: Cited from: R. T. Rockafellar, Monotone operators and the proximal point algorithm, SIAM J. Control Optim., 14 (1976), pp. 877-898, Proposition 3.

items.name: COROLLARY 3.2
items.statement: If $y_k$ is chosen as in (2.18) and $\alpha_k$ is chosen as in (2.21), then $$\varphi_{k+1}^*+(1-\alpha_k)\delta_k\geq f(J_{\lambda_k}y_k)+\frac1{2\lambda_k}\|J_{\lambda_k}y_k-y_k\|^2=\phi_k^*. \tag{3.8}$$

items.name: COROLLARY 2.2
items.statement: If $y_{k}$ is chosen as in (2.18), $x_{k+1}$ is chosen as in (2.20), and $\alpha_{k}$ is chosen as in (2.21), then $$\varphi_ {k + 1} ^ {*} \geq f (x _ {k + 1}) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda_ {k}} \left\| y _ {k} - x _ {k + 1} \right\| ^ {2} \geq f (x _ {k + 1}). \tag {2.22}$$

items.name: THE PROXIMAL POINT ALGORITHM
items.statement:
Initialization. Choose a feasible starting point $x_0 \in \mathbf{R}^n$ ($f(x_0)<\infty$), and constants $\lambda_0>0$ and $A>0$. Define $
u_0:=x_0$, $A_0:=A$. Step $k$, $k\geq0$: (a) Choose $\lambda_k>0$, and calculate $\alpha_k>0$ from $\alpha_k^2=(1-\alpha_k)A_k\lambda_k$, that is, $$\alpha_ {k} =  rac {\sqrt {(A _ {k} \lambda_ {k}) ^ {2} + 4 A _ {k} \lambda_ {k}} - A _ {k} \lambda_ {k}}{2}. 	ag {2.23}$$ (b) Define $$ egin{aligned}y_k&=(1-\alpha_k)x_k+\alpha_k
u_k,\x_{k+1}&:=J_{\lambda_k}y_k=\arg\min_{z\in\mathbf R^n}\{f(z)+(1/(2\lambda_k))\|z-y_k\|^2\},\end{aligned} 	ag {2.24}$$ $$
u_{k+1}=
u_k+(1/\alpha_k)(x_{k+1}-y_k),\qquad A_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)A_k.$$

items.name: THE MONOTONIC PROXIMAL POINT ALGORITHM
items.statement:
Initialization. Choose a feasible starting point $x_0\in\mathbf R^n$ ($f(x_0)<\infty$), and constants $\lambda_0>0$ and $A>0$. Define $
u_0:=x_0$, $A_0:=A$. Step $k$, $k\geq0$: choose $\lambda_k>0$ and set $$\alpha_k= rac{\sqrt{(A_k\lambda_k)^2+4A_k\lambda_k}-A_k\lambda_k}{2}.$$ Define $$y_k=(1-\alpha_k)x_k+\alpha_k
u_k,$$ $$ ar x_{k+1}=J_{\lambda_k}y_k:=\arg\min_{z\in\mathbf R^n}\{f(z)+(1/(2\lambda_k))\|z-y_k\|^2\},$$ $$x_{k+1}=\arg\min\{f( ar x_{k+1}),f(x_k)\},$$ $$
u_{k+1}=
u_k+(1/\alpha_k)(x_{k+1}-y_k),\qquad A_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)A_k.$$

items.name: LEMMA 2.2
items.statement: $$\frac {1}{(1 + \sqrt {A} \sum_ {j = 0} ^ {k - 1} \sqrt {\lambda_ {j}}) ^ {2}} \leqq \beta_ {k} \leqq \frac {1}{(1 + (\sqrt {A} / 2) \sum_ {j = 0} ^ {k - 1} \sqrt {\lambda_ {j}}) ^ {2}}. \tag {2.25}$$
items.proof: Proof. Put $\beta_k=\mu_k^{-2}$. From $\beta_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)\beta_k$, $A_{k+1}=\beta_{k+1}A$, and (2.21), one obtains $$\mu_{k+1}^2-\mu_k^2=\mu_{k+1}\sqrt{A\lambda_k}. \tag{2.26}$$ The inequality $2\mu_{k+1}(\mu_{k+1}-\mu_k)\geq\mu_{k+1}^2-\mu_k^2$ gives $\mu_{k+1}-\mu_k\geq\sqrt{A\lambda_k}/2$; summing and using $\mu_0=1$ proves the upper bound. Since $\mu_{k+1}\geq\mu_k$, the reverse comparison gives $\mu_{k+1}-\mu_k\leq\sqrt{A\lambda_k}$; summing proves the lower bound.

items.name: THEOREM 3.1
items.statement: If, in the algorithm in §2, $x_{k+1}$ is calculated according to criterion A' instead of (2.20), then $$f(x_k)\leq\varphi_k^*+\delta_k, \tag{3.9}$$ where $\{\delta_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ satisfies $$\delta_0=0,\quad\delta_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)\delta_k+\frac{\varepsilon_k^2}{2\lambda_k},\quad k=0,1,\dots. \tag{3.10}$$
items.proof: Proof. We prove (3.9) and (3.10) by induction. Since $f(x_0)=\varphi_0^*$, they are true for $k=0$. Suppose they hold for $k$. From (3.8) and Lemma 3.1, $$\varphi_{k+1}^*+(1-\alpha_k)\delta_k\geq\phi_k^*\geq\phi_k(x_{k+1})-\frac{\varepsilon_k^2}{2\lambda_k}=f(x_{k+1})+\frac1{2\lambda_k}\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|^2-\frac{\varepsilon_k^2}{2\lambda_k},$$ which implies the assertion. This proves the theorem. $\square$

items.name: LEMMA 3.3
items.statement: The solution to (3.10) is $$\delta_k=\frac{\beta_k}{2}\cdot\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{\varepsilon_j^2/\lambda_j}{\beta_{j+1}}. \tag{3.12}$$ Moreover, $$\delta_k\leqq2\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{\lambda_j}\left(\frac{1+\sqrt A\sum_{i=0}^j\sqrt{\lambda_i}}{1+\sqrt A\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\sqrt{\lambda_j}}\right)^2. \tag{3.13}$$ Assume $\lambda_i\leq M\lambda_j$ whenever $i\leq j$, (3.14), and $\varepsilon_k=O(1/k^\sigma)$, $k=1,2,\dots$, for some $\sigma>0$, (3.15). Then $$\delta_k=O(1/k^{2\sigma-1}). \tag{3.16}$$
items.proof: Proof. Divide $\delta_{j+1}=(\beta_{j+1}/\beta_j)\delta_j+\varepsilon_j^2/(2\lambda_j)$ by $\beta_{j+1}$ to obtain (3.17), sum for $j=0,1,\ldots,k-1$, and use $\delta_0=0$ to obtain (3.12). Inequality (3.13) follows from the lower bound in Lemma 2.2. Under (3.14), the estimates in the paper give $$\delta_k\leq\bar c\,\frac{\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(j\varepsilon_j)^2}{k^2}. \tag{3.18}$$ Condition (3.15) bounds the numerator by $\tilde c\int_0^k t^{2-2\sigma}dt=\tilde c k^{3-2\sigma}/(3-2\sigma)$, proving (3.16).

items.name: THEOREM 2.2
items.statement: For any feasible point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the proximal point algorithm stated above has the global convergence rate estimate $$\begin{aligned} f (x _ {k}) - f (x) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda_ {k - 1}} \| y _ {k - 1} - x _ {k} \| ^ {2} &\leq \frac {f (x _ {0}) - f (x) + (A / 2) \| x - x _ {0} \| ^ {2}}{(1 + (\sqrt {A} / 2) \sum_ {j = 0} ^ {k - 1} \sqrt {\lambda_ {j}}) ^ {2}} \tag {2.27} \\ &= O \left(\frac {1}{(\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\sqrt{\lambda_j})^2}\right).\end{aligned}$$

items.name: THEOREM 3.2
items.statement: In the modified proximal point algorithm in which the point $x_k$ is calculated according to criterion A', we have for any $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $$f(x_k)-f(x)\leq\beta_k(\varphi_0(x)-f(x))+\delta_k,$$ where $\{\delta_k\}$ satisfies (3.10). In particular, $$f(x_k)-f^*\leq\beta_k\left(f(x_0)-f^*+\frac A2\rho(x_0,X^*)^2\right)+\delta_k. \tag{3.11}$$

items.name: THEOREM 2.3
items.statement: Suppose $f$ has a minimizer $x^*$ and $f^*=f(x^*)=\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}f(z)$. Denote the set of minimizers of $f$ by $X^*$. The proximal point algorithm above possesses the global convergence rate estimate $$f(x_k)-f^*\leq\frac{4}{A(\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\sqrt{\lambda_j})^2}\left(f(x_0)-f^*+\frac A2\rho(x_0,X^*)^2\right). \tag{2.28}$$ The algorithm converges, that is, $f(x_k)\to f^*$ if $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sqrt{\lambda_k}=\infty. \tag{2.29}$$ In particular, if $\lambda_k\cong\lambda>0$, $$\begin{aligned}f(x_k)-f^*&\leq\frac{4/(A\lambda)}{k^2}\left(f(x_0)-f^*+\frac A2\rho(x_0,X^*)^2\right)\tag{2.30}\\&=O(1/k^2).\end{aligned}$$

items.name: THEOREM 3.3
items.statement: Consider a proximal point algorithm that differs from the one stated in §2 only in that $x_k$ is approximately calculated according to criterion $\mathbf A'$ with an error $\varepsilon_k$. Assume errors satisfy (3.15) for some $\sigma>1/2$, and parameters satisfy (3.14). Then, for any feasible $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $$f(x_k)-f(x)\leq O(1/k^2)+O(1/k^{2\sigma-1})\to0.$$ In particular, $$f(x_k)-f^*=O(1/k^2)+O(1/k^{2\sigma-1}),$$ and if $\sigma\geq3/2$, $$f(x_k)-f^*=O(1/k^2).$$
items.proof: It is obtained from Theorem 3.2 and Lemmas 2.2 and 3.3.

items.name: COROLLARY 2.3
items.statement: If (2.29) holds true in the proximal point algorithm, then $$\frac{\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|^2}{\lambda_k}\to0. \tag{2.32}$$ If $\{\lambda_k\}$ is bounded from above, then $\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|\to0$. (2.33) Also, $\lambda_k\rho(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))^2\to0$. (2.34) If $\{\lambda_k\}$ is bounded away from 0, then $\rho(0,\partial f(x_k))\to0$. (2.35) If $f$ is differentiable, (2.35) means that $\|f'(x_k)\|\to0$. (2.36)

items.name: Remark 2.4
items.statement:
The convergence rate (2.26) for the accelerated proximal point algorithm compares favorably with the classical proximal point estimate

$$
f(x_k)-f^*\leq \frac{d(x_0,X^*)^2}{2\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\lambda_j}.
$$

The new denominator grows like the square of $\sum_j\sqrt{\lambda_j}$.

items.name: THEOREM 4.1
items.statement: Suppose $f$ has no minimizers or is unbounded from below. The original proximal point algorithms in §§2 and 3, and their monotonic versions discussed above, minimize $f$, that is, $$\lim_{k\to\infty}f(x_k)=\inf_{x\in\mathbf R^n}f(x). \tag{4.1}$$
items.proof: Proof. Since the algorithm in §2 is a special case of the algorithm in §3, we prove (4.1) only for the latter. The proofs for the monotonic versions are similar. First consider $f^*>-\infty$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, take $x^\varepsilon$ satisfying $f(x^\varepsilon)-f^*\leq\varepsilon/2$. For large $k$, (3.23) gives $f(x_k)-f(x^\varepsilon)\leq\varepsilon/2$, hence $f(x_k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon$. If $f^*=-\infty$, let $M$ be arbitrary and choose $x^M$ satisfying $f(x^M)\leq M$. For large $k$, (3.23) gives $f(x_k)-f(x^M)\leq\varepsilon$, hence $f(x_k)\leq M+\varepsilon$ and (4.1) follows.

items.name: Remark 3.1
items.statement: Rockafellar's inexact proximal point result gives convergence of iterates to a zero of a maximal monotone operator under summable errors. Section 3 instead records objective-value estimates for criterion $\mathbf A'$ and compares their error requirements with those classical criteria.
